text:
Andrew: heads up — customer on Android 12 (Pixel 4a) reports SSE stream drops mid-response when switching from 5G -> home Wi‑Fi. They see partial JSON and then the stream just stops. No 500s on our side.

Support: can you paste the client logs and the server request id? also which model/route?

Andrew: route: /v1/streams/generate, model: redwood-small, request id: req_0b9f2c. Client log snippet from the app:

```
2026-03-11 18:22:14.342 com.acme.speech D/Stream: recv chunk {"delta":"hello"}
2026-03-11 18:22:15.128 com.acme.speech D/Network: connectivity change: MOBILE -> WIFI
2026-03-11 18:22:15.220 com.acme.speech D/Stream: recv chunk {"delta":" there"}
2026-03-11 18:22:15.340 com.acme.speech W/Stream: no data for 3s
2026-03-11 18:22:18.342 com.acme.speech E/Stream: connection closed by peer, bytes total=1024
```

Devon: I pulled logs for req_0b9f2c — server got the full POST and started streaming. No stacktrace. The LB (nginx) shows a downstream RST around the same time. Extract from LB: `upstream_response_time: 3.01, downstream: 0.00, tcp_fin:1` — hmm.

Maria: @Devon can you paste the raw nginx access and error lines? upstream RST could be client-side or an intermediate resetting MSS.

Devon: pasted below. Note weird MSS clamping in the tcpdump from that region (customer’s ISP).

```
# nginx access
2876543210 - - [11/Mar/2026:18:22:18 +0000] "GET /v1/streams/generate?id=req_0b9f2c HTTP/1.1" 200 0 "-" "acme-client/3.2" rt=3.012
# nginx error
2026/03/11 18:22:18 [info] 12345#0: *67890 client prematurely closed connection, client: 10.10.10.50, server: inference, request: "GET /v1/streams/generate?id=req_0b9f2c HTTP/1.1", host: "api.redwood.com"
```

```
# tcpdump from LB interface
12:22:15.220 IP 5g-client -> lb: Flags [P.], seq 100:464, ack 200, win 43690, length 364, MSS 1452
12:22:15.224 IP wifi-client -> lb: Flags [P.], seq 100:464, ack 200, win 64240, length 364, MSS 1360
12:22:18.342 IP wifi-client -> lb: Flags [R], seq 464, ack 564, win 0, length 0
```

SREBot: automated note — no server exception, connection terminated by client or intermediate RST.

Tina: this screams PMTU/MSS clamping during the NAT/handoff. Android switching networks can expose an MTU mismatch and some home routers clamp MSS causing fragments to be dropped — then the client TCP stack might force RST or drop the socket.

Support: customer says it reproduces reliably when they toggle Wi‑Fi on/off while a large stream is in-flight. small streams OK.

Andrew: action ideas: (1) try forcing smaller server-side chunk sizes or send periodic comment frames to keep TCP alive, (2) add explicit keepalive/heartbeat from server every 1s, (3) recommend client enable HTTP/1.1 TCP keepalive and set SO_KEEPALIVE shorter on Android, (4) provide repro steps to customer with socat/tc to simulate MSS clamp.

Maria: can we check if our proxy (nginx) has sendfile or tcp_nopush flags that might coalesce packets -> bigger segment that gets dropped? Also check if ALPN -> HTTP/2? This route is HTTP/1.1 SSE.

Devon: nginx config snippet for that host: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ''; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` — nothing obviously buffering. We can try a deploy to add periodic 128‑byte keepalive comments (`: keepalive\n\n`) every 2s for long streams.

SREBot: suggested: set `tcp_keepalive_time=60` on nodes serving mobile regions. Will open infra ticket if agreed.

Tina: also useful to give customer a client-side mitigation: when they detect network change, recreate the stream (resume with last token) rather than relying on midstream TCP survival. Provide guidance for idempotent resume using last-event-id header.

Support: can you draft repro commands for them? They asked for a reproducible binary test rather than full app changes.

Andrew: yes — send them these steps:
1) on linux machine, create a small server that streams a large response: `python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 0.0.0.0` then use a script to `for i in {1..10000}; do echo ": chunk $i"; sleep 0.1; done` piping to response.
2) use `tc` to clamp MSS on interface: `sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem loss 0%` then `sudo iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1360` to simulate router clamping.
3) from another terminal, start a persistent curl: `curl -N http://server:8000/stream` and toggle network interface (ifup/ifdown or switch from tether to wifi). Should reproduce silent close.

Devon: I'll prepare a short reproducer image and run it against our staging behind the same LB to confirm. If confirmed, we can ship keepalive comments as a short-term server-side mitigation.

Tina: long term, platform should detect lots of downstream RSTs on network-change events and surface them as a metric and maybe trigger a streaming policy that uses smaller chunks / more frequent flushes for mobile user-agents.

Support: customer ok to test server-side keepalive change if we provide a staging flag.

Andrew: assigning to @Devon to run repro + quick patch to send `:ka\n` comments every 1.5s for streams > 10s. Please update thread with results.

Devon: started running repro locally, will post logs shortly.

(--- later)

Devon: repro confirmed on staging. With MSS clamped to 1360 and network flip, stream stalls and LB sees downstream RST. With keepalive comments every 1.5s the connection stays up and client receives final chunks.

Support: passing mitigation to customer with steps and expected behavioural change.

Andrew: thanks everyone. Will follow up to schedule infra ticket for `tcp_keepalive_time` and an observability alert for RST spikes from mobile agents.

Support: closing from support side once customer verifies. :thumbsup:
